subject: Request: clarification on per-token billing, commit tiers, and CSV usage export
messages:
From: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@elarahealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: accounts@elarahealth.com
Date: Wed, 8 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Quick ask: per-token line items + commit tier options

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the demo last week — Elara's engineering and data teams were impressed with the latency and cost controls. Before we take this to procurement, we need two things clarified on the billing side so we can map to our finance model:  

1) Detailed invoice line items: our accounting team needs a CSV (or similar) that breaks monthly charges into per-model per-token tallies, plus a separate line for any infrastructure/overage fees. A single monthly total isn’t sufficient for our reconciliation.

2) Commit/discount mechanics: you mentioned volume discounts tied to commit tiers during the demo. Can you provide the exact per-token pricing at 0 (no commit), 1M, 5M, and 20M token monthly commit levels, and whether unused commit credits roll over or expire? Also, how do overages get billed if we exceed a committed tier mid-month?

I've attached a small sample of our June traffic export (elara_usage_q2_2026_sample.csv) to illustrate what level of granularity we need. Procurement has a strict cutoff on July 16, so any timing constraints would be helpful.

Appreciate your help — cc'ing our billing address.

Thanks,
Sam Taylor
Head of Engineering
Elara Health

---
Attachment: elara_usage_q2_2026_sample.csv (CSV, 28KB)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@elarahealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Jul 2026 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick ask: per-token line items + commit tier options

Hi Sam —

Thanks for the sample and the clear asks. High level answers up front: yes, we can provide a per-model, per-token CSV export on a monthly cadence, and we have defined commit tiers with clear overage rules. A few quick clarifying questions so I give exactly what procurement needs:

- For the CSV: do you prefer a single file per month (our standard) or split by model/service? We can include columns for model_id, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens, region, and route_id. We can also include a cost column computed at the active effective per-token rate for that day.

- For commit behavior: do you want commits to be applied at the organization level across projects, or scoped to a single project/route? We support both but pricing and rollover policies differ slightly.

I'll loop in Vivek on the formal pricing tiers and Logan on the invoice-format specifics. If it's helpful, I can draft the CSV layout and the commit tier table and send both by EOD tomorrow so procurement has something to review before your July 16 cutoff.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Phone: +1-415-555-0192

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@elarahealth.com>, accounts@elarahealth.com
Date: Thu, 9 Jul 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Quick ask: per-token line items + commit tier options

Logan — can you and finance confirm we can produce the CSV with the following columns and default behaviors? I sketched a sample below and attached the proposed commit tiers doc. Procurement at Elara needs the file format and sample output to reconcile to their GL. They specifically asked for: model_id, model_name, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens, effective_per_token_rate, cost_usd, billing_region, route_id, and invoice_line_item_id.

Proposed commit tiers (proposal attached):
- No commit: $0.00060 / token (on-demand)
- 1M monthly commit: $0.00048 / token (20% off on-demand)
- 5M monthly commit: $0.00036 / token (40% off)
- 20M monthly commit: $0.00030 / token (50% off)

Key questions for finance to confirm:
1) If customer purchases a 5M monthly commit at org-level and uses 6.2M tokens in a month, do we bill 5M at commit rate and the 1.2M overage at the next tier rate or at on-demand? (procurement will need deterministic rules)
2) What is our default roll-over policy for unused commits? (Expire vs 30-day rollover vs permanent)
3) Can we export invoice_line_item_id to tie to each CSV row? That helps their accounting team reconcile line-by-line.

Thanks — Sam's procurement deadline is July 16. Can finance provide a final CSV sample and a short note on rollover/overage behavior by Friday EOD?

Rachel

Attachment: proposed_commit_tiers.pdf (PDF, 12KB)

---
Quoted message included below.

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@elarahealth.com>, accounts@elarahealth.com
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick ask: per-token line items + commit tier options

Hi all —

Thanks for the clear framing. Finance confirms we can produce the requested CSV with the exact columns Rachel listed. A few binding policy points below (final pricing authority is sales + rev ops but these are our default behaviors):

1) Overage billing: commits are consumed first at the committed rate. Any overage within the billing month is billed at the on-demand rate (no automatic "next-tier" discount unless a custom addendum is signed). Example: 5M commit used 6.2M tokens => 5M @ commit rate, 1.2M @ on-demand.

2) Rollover: standard policy is expiration at month-end (no roll-over). We can offer a 30-day rollover for enterprise deals as a contractual amendment (typical for Dedicated/Private customers).

3) invoice_line_item_id: yes, we will surface a stable invoice_line_item_id per aggregated row. The CSV will include both the invoice_line_item_id and the originating request ids for traceability.

4) File format & delivery: we will produce a monthly CSV export, zipped, and available via secure S3 link; we can also push directly to the customer's SFTP on request.

Vivek — for this particular deal (DW-9342), the pricing table Rachel proposed looks reasonable as a starting point. We recommend offering a 30-day trial of 1M commit at the 1M rate to validate traffic, then convert to org-level commit if they opt in.

Sam — I attached an example CSV row (first three rows) to show the field mapping. If that looks good, Rachel/Vivek can circulate the exact formal proposal with those commit tiers and the no-rollover default called out.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Finance Manager, Redwood Inference
logan_wright@redwood.ai
